title: Get the deploy tool's crontab and signed string right to the byte

blocks.text: The deploy tool produces two pieces of text, and both have bitten the team.

items: The **crontab** it installs on every host has a header line and three jobs. The host's installer rejects a crontab unless every line, the last one included, ends with a line break, and last week it rejected ours.

For each request to the artifact gateway, the tool signs a **string to sign**: the method, the path and the date, one per line. The gateway computes its HMAC over exactly those characters, with nothing after the date, and answers `403` when the two signatures differ.

blocks.text: Write both methods in `src/main/java/practice/DeployTexts.java` as text blocks; the javadoc of `crontab()` lists its lines. The tests compare the exact characters each method returns, with requests of their own. About ten lines in total.

cases.says: the crontab holds the header and the three jobs, one per line, in order
the string to sign holds the method, the path and the date of the request, one per line
the crontab's last line ends with a line break, like every other line
the string to sign ends with the date, with no line break after it

origin.section: The Closing Delimiter's Line Decides Whether the Value Ends With a Newline

concepts: A closing delimiter on its own line ends the value with a newline; on the last content line it leaves none.
